rendered: The review does not recommend this. It says the opposite: dissolving the aluminium foil in an alkaline solution is not a sustainable way to separate the cathode materials. The stated reason is that recovering current collectors such as Cu and Al matters because Cu smelting is a key source of emissions in the cradle-to-gate stages of the battery life cycle.[1][2] suggesting that dissolving Al[3]in an alkaline solution is not a sustainable separation method[4]. Alkaline leaching is also described elsewhere as a process with environmental drawbacks, including wastewater concerns and costly waste processing. The review's own recommendations for separating cathode from Al foil instead centre on binder removal with greener solvents, or on delamination in media such as ethylene glycol.
